land.text: the Duchy of Croatia of Tomislav's Croats of Dalmatia and Pannonia, raised to a kingdom c. 925

predecessors.note: The main page: 'Elevation to kingdom: c. 925'; 'It is generally said that Tomislav was crowned in 925, but it is not known when or by whom.'

land.text: the Kingdom of Croatia in union with Hungary after Coloman's coronation at Biograd in 1102: the kingdom's last Cliopatria shape, 1094-1098

successors.note: Infobox: 'Succession crisis and coronation of King Coloman of Hungary: 1102'; successor 'Kingdom of Croatia in union with Hungary'. Slavonia had been Hungarian since 1091.

capitals.name: Nin
capitals.note: The main page: 'There was no permanent state capital, as the royal residence varied from one ruler to another.' It lists Nin among the royal seats but gives no ruler for 925-948; Nin is the listed seat nearest the founding, a placeholder. Reopened after review: the Trpimirovic dynasty page lists no seats for 928-948 (it names Klis and a royal estate between Trogir and Split), so the placeholder stays.

capitals.name: Solin
capitals.note: The main page lists Solin as a seat of Michael Kresimir II (949-969).

capitals.name: Biograd na Moru
capitals.note: Listed as a seat of Drzislav (969-997) and of Petar Kresimir IV (1058-1074), who also kept Nin (15.18E, 44.24N) and for a time Sibenik. The pages say nothing for 998-1057; the seat is carried over. Reopened: the main page names Biograd as a seat of Drzislav and Kresimir IV only; 998-1057 stays carried over.

capitals.name: Knin
capitals.note: Seat of Zvonimir (1075-1089; the Zvonimir page: 'ruled from the city of Knin') and of Petar Snacic (1093-1097). The last king was killed at Gvozd in 1097; Coloman was crowned at Biograd in 1102.

rulers.name: Tomislav
rulers.title: duke from c. 910, king by 925
rulers.note: Tomislav page: duke c. 910, crowned 924 or 925, 'last documented appearance' 928; the Trpimirovic dynasty page (reopened after review) gives 925-928.

rulers.name: Svetoslav Suronja
rulers.note: Trpimirovic dynasty page: 'Svetoslav Suronja (997-1000)', Drzislav's eldest son and co-ruler (Stephen Drzislav page); the main page's 'violent contest for the throne' has no further names.

rulers.name: Kresimir III
rulers.note: 997-1000: Drzislav's three sons contest the throne (main page). The Trpimirovic dynasty page lists Gojslav (1000-c. 1020) in parallel to Kresimir III (1000-c. 1030).

rulers.name: Petar Kresimir IV
rulers.note: The Peter Kresimir IV page: died 1074 or 1075; crowned 1059.

rulers.name: Petar Snacic
rulers.note: Elected king by the Croatian lords in 1093 while Ladislaus's Hungarians held Slavonia; killed at Gvozd 1097.

correction.text: Tomislav's realm: 'the Croats of Pannonia and Dalmatia'; Fine, quoted on the page: modern Croatia, Slavonia, northern and western Bosnia and the Dalmatian coast from Rijeka to the Cetina, excluding the Byzantine towns

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's kingdom shape begins in 926 but the Tomislav page has him king of the united Croats of Pannonia and Dalmatia by 925 ('crowned 924 or 925'; Council of Split 925). The 926 shape is applied one year early. The infobox gives no area.

55.5 thousand km2. The Tomislav page describes the realm (Fine) as Croatia, Slavonia, northern and western Bosnia and the coast from Rijeka to the Cetina, and notes other historians reach further into Bosnia; the main page has no infobox area. Shape accepted.

56.2 thousand km2, slightly further south (43.08N). Unverified: page budget; no page opened dates a change in 936, and the main page records nothing territorial between Tomislav (928) and Michael Kresimir II (949-969) except that Kresimir 'restored order throughout most of the state'.
A one-year Cliopatria shape of 54.8 thousand km2 between two near-identical shapes. Unverified: page budget.
55.7 thousand km2; Michael Kresimir II (949-969) 'restored order throughout most of the state'. Unverified: page budget.
55.0 thousand km2 under Stephen Drzislav (969-997), who 'established better relations with the Byzantine Empire and their Theme of Dalmatia'. Unverified: page budget.

Jumps to 90.3 thousand km2 (+35 thousand) with the bbox unchanged east and west: Cliopatria fills in Bosnia. No page opened dates this; the Tomislav page says historians differ widely on how far into Bosnia the kingdom reached (Fine: about a third of the eastern claim is 'entirely speculation'). Kept with the ledger's confidence-1 event for 980; this is the largest unverified step of the dossier. Reopened (Stephen Drzislav page): silent on 980 and on Bosnia; still unexplained.

92.8 thousand km2. After Drzislav's death in 997 'his three sons ... opened a violent contest for the throne', which let the Bulgarians under Samuil 'encroach on the Croatian possessions along the Adriatic' (undated on the page). Unverified: page budget.

90.4 thousand km2, 2.4 thousand less than 990. 'After 1000, Orseolo led the Venetian fleet into the eastern Adriatic and gradually took control of the whole of it'; Kresimir III (1000-1030) 'tried to restore the Dalmatian cities and had some success until 1018'. The slight loss is consistent with this; the cities are handled by the contest events.

minus.text: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Croatia shape of 1018
the Dalmatian cities Zadar, Split and Trogir

correction.text: the kingdom without the Dalmatian city-states Zadar, Split and Trogir, 1018-1059 (they were not Croatian until 1060); Biograd and Nin stay Croatian

keyframe_review.note: 1018: Kresimir III was defeated by Venice and 'his kingdom briefly became a vassal of the Byzantine Empire until 1025'. The page has Petar Kresimir IV 'gain control over the Dalmatian city-states' only from 1060 (Byzantium recognised him in 1069, Peter Kresimir page). Cliopatria draws one constant 90.4 thousand km2 shape for 1018-1084; the corrected shape for 1018-1059 leaves out the Dalmatian cities. New keyframes 1060 and 1074 follow. Corrected after review: the 1018 shape used to remove a 30 km circle round Zadar labelled 'Zadar, Biograd and Nin', which took the capital Biograd (25 km from Zadar) and Nin out; only Zadar (15 km), Split and Trogir are removed now.

correction.text: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Croatia shape of 1018

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: with Petar Kresimir IV 'the medieval Croatian kingdom reached its territorial peak' and from 1060 he 'gained control over the Dalmatian city-states'. Cliopatria's 1018 shape unchanged for 1060-1073. Held to 1068; the 1069 keyframe adds the islands.

union.text: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Croatia shape of 1018
the Kvarner island city-states Krk, Rab and Cres

correction.text: the 1060 kingdom plus the Kvarner island city-states Krk, Rab and Cres recognised by Byzantium in 1069

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 1069, Byzantium 'recognize[s] him as supreme ruler of the parts of Dalmatia' (Peter Kresimir IV page); the Theme of Dalmatia page lists Krk, Cres and Rab among the theme's city-states. Cliopatria's 1018 shape does not reach the islands, so they are added as circles. Held to 1073; the Normans take the mainland cities in 1074.

minus.text: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Croatia shape of 1018
the Dalmatian cities Zadar, Split, Trogir, Biograd and Nin

union.text: the kingdom without the Dalmatian cities taken by the Normans
the Kvarner island city-states Krk, Rab and Cres

correction.text: the kingdom without the mainland Dalmatian cities Zadar, Split, Trogir, Biograd and Nin taken by the Normans in 1074-1075, keeping the Kvarner islands (Zvonimir's authority reached 'as far as the distant town of Osor')

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Normans under Count Amico captured Kresimir in 1074-1075 and the ransom gave up Zadar, Split, Trogir and the capitals Biograd and Nin; Venice expelled the Normans in February 1075 (Zvonimir page) and 'secured the cities for itself' (main page). The cities leave the Croatian shape from 1074 and are contested until 1085. Cliopatria keeps them in its 1018 shape to 1084. Reopened after review: the page names Zadar, Split, Trogir, Biograd and Nin (and 'both capitals'), so the 30 km circle round Zadar stays here; the islands Krk, Rab and Cres added in 1069 stay Croatian to 1084 and leave with the 1085 transfer of Byzantine rights to Venice.

70.1 thousand km2, 20 thousand less than 1084 with the eastern bbox edge pulled in. The main page gives 1085 only as the year 'the Byzantines transferred their rights in Dalmatia to Venice' (after Zvonimir's naval help to the Normans); it does not say Croatia lost land that year, and the cities alone are smaller than 20 thousand km2. Kept as drawn; holds 1085-1090, since the Hungarian conquest of Slavonia is dated 1091. Reopened (Zvonimir page): silent on territory 1085-1089 ('The page gives no details on changes in the east'); only 'by the end of 1091 [Ladislaus] conquered a big part of Slavonia'. The 20 thousand km2 drop stays unexplained and is Cliopatria's; the Kvarner islands leave in 1085 (see the 1085 loss).

correction.text: the kingdom south of the Gvozd mountain after Ladislaus took Slavonia in 1091: the 1094 shape held for 1091-1102

keyframe_review.note: 35.5 thousand km2: Slavonia and the north are gone. The page dates the loss to 1091 ('In 1091 Ladislaus crossed the Drava river and conquered the entire province of Slavonia'), not to Cliopatria's 1094, and the kingdom lasts until Coloman's coronation in 1102, four years after the shape ends. Corrected: the same shape for 1091-1102.

region.text: the Croats of Pannonia and Dalmatia

ledger.note: 925: Tomislav is crowned King of the Croats and unites Pannonia and Dalmatia. 'It is generally said that Tomislav was crowned in 925'; Pope John X calls him 'King of the Croats'; 'Sometime between 923 and 928, Tomislav succeeded in uniting the Croats of Pannonia and Dalmatia' (main page). The year is the page's; the land is Cliopatria's 926 shape.

region.text: part of the former Pannonian duchy, including Sisak

ledger.note: c. 925: Croatia keeps its northern borders against the Magyars and gains part of the former Pannonian duchy. 'Croatia kept its northern borders and gained part of the former Pannonian duchy, including Sisak'; the Hungarian conflict is 'not precisely dated'.

region.text: probably eastern Bosnia, where the Bulgarian army was destroyed

ledger.note: 926: Tomislav destroys Simeon's army under Alogobotur. 'Tomislav destroys the army of Bulgarian Duke Alogobotur at the Croatian-Bulgarian battle of 926, probably in eastern Bosnia'; Bulgaria had destroyed the Principality of Serbia in 924.

region.text: the Bosnian marches fought over in 926

ledger.note: 927: Simeon dies and peace is restored. 'Simeon I dies [927]. Pope John X sends legates ... to restore peace between Croatia and Bulgaria.' Croatia loses nothing.

region.text: Cliopatria's 980 shape without its 979 shape: the added interior, Bosnia

ledger.note: 980: page silent. Cliopatria's shape grows from 55.0 to 90.3 thousand km2 (Bosnia filled in) in 980; no page opened dates or explains it. A gap for the gap-fillers; the Tomislav page says the realm already reached northern and western Bosnia and historians differ on the rest. Reopened (Stephen Drzislav page): silent on 980 and on Bosnia; it says Zachlumia 'was a part of the Kingdom of Croatia, before and after Stephen Drzislav', that a 13th-century chronicle's 'ruled over Croatia and Bosnia' is about his father Michael Kresimir II, and that after Samuil's 986 campaign towards Zadar 'the cities were returned to Croatian control'. The jump stays unexplained.

region.text: the Dalmatian cities Zadar, Split and Trogir taken by Orseolo

ledger.note: 1000: Venice's Orseolo takes the Adriatic. 'After 1000, Orseolo led the Venetian fleet into the eastern Adriatic and gradually took control of the whole of it'; Kresimir III 'tried to restore the Dalmatian cities and had some success until 1018'. Region narrowed from the four-county gazetteer region 'Dalmatia' to the three cities the page names for 1000 (Zadar, Trogir, Split).

region.text: the Dalmatian cities Zadar, Split and Trogir lost in 1018

ledger.note: 1018: Venice defeats Kresimir III; the kingdom becomes a Byzantine vassal until 1025. 'The same year his kingdom briefly became a vassal of the Byzantine Empire until 1025.' The Byzantine side of the vassalage (1018-1025) belongs in the byzantine-empire dossier.

region.text: the Dalmatian cities Zadar, Split and Trogir

ledger.note: 1018: the Dalmatian cities pass out of Croatian hands. Kresimir III 'tried to restore the Dalmatian cities and had some success until 1018'; Venice defeated him that year. Counterpart Venice is the page's winner; the cities were nominally Byzantine, as the page has Byzantium recognising Peter Kresimir IV there in 1069. Region (fix after review): Zadar, Split and Trogir only, the cities the page names for 1000; no page names Biograd or Nin for 1018 and Biograd stays the royal seat to 1074, so they stay in the kingdom. Zadar radius 15 km because the r5 grid (cell spacing about 16 km) has no land cell centre within 10 km of Zadar; Biograd is 25 km away.

region.text: the Narentine duchy (Pagania), the southern Dalmatian coast between the Cetina and the Neretva

ledger.note: 1050: the Narentine duke becomes a vassal of Stjepan I. Stjepan I 'only went so far as to get the Narentine duke to become his vassal in 1050.' Pagania lay between the Cetina and the Neretva.

region.text: the Dalmatian cities Zadar, Split and Trogir

ledger.note: 1060: Petar Kresimir IV takes the Dalmatian city-states. The kingdom is called 'Kingdom of Croatia and Dalmatia' 'only from 1060 when king Peter Krešimir IV gained control over the Dalmatian city-states'; its influence also reached 'the closest southern Dalmatian duchy of Pagania', 'Zahumlje, Travunia, and Duklja' (not annexations; no vassalage is stated). Region (fix after review): Zadar, Split and Trogir; Biograd and Nin were never lost in 1018 (see the 1018 loss), and the page says only 'the Dalmatian city-states'.

region.text: parts of the Kvarner coast and eastern Istria

ledger.note: 1067: Ulric I of Carniola occupies the Kvarner coast and eastern Istria. 'Ulric I, Margrave of Carniola, occupied parts of the Kvarner coast and eastern Istria. His ban, Demetrius Zvonimir, later liberated these areas.' The Zvonimir page dates the Carantanian occupation 'around 1063' (Chronicon Pictum); the Peter Kresimir IV page's 1067 is kept.

union.text: the Kvarner island city-states Krk, Rab and Cres

region.text: the parts of Dalmatia Byzantium had controlled: the cities Zadar, Split and Trogir and the Kvarner island city-states Krk, Rab and Cres

ledger.note: 1069: Byzantium recognises Petar Kresimir IV in Dalmatia. 'he had the Byzantine Empire recognize him as supreme ruler of the parts of Dalmatia' (Peter Kresimir IV page, 1069); he styles his realm 'regnum Dalmatiae et Chroatia'. Region (fix after review): the theme's own towns, not the four-county gazetteer region 'Dalmatia' (which would add Ragusa, Peljesac and the Neretva delta). The Theme of Dalmatia page names its eight original city-states as Krk (Vecla), Cres (Crespa), Rab (Arba), Zadar, Trogir, Split, Ragusa and Kotor, and says Byzantine control had collapsed by the 1060s everywhere except Ragusa and the southern third of Dalmatia; so Ragusa and Kotor are left out. The page does not list the towns recognised in 1069: the list is the reviewer's reading, checked against the Theme page. Krk, Rab and Cres are drawn as 12-20 km circles on their town coordinates (Wikipedia: Krk 45 01 N 14 34 E, Rab 44 45 N 14 45 E, Cres 44 57 N 14 24 E).

region.text: the Kvarner coast and eastern Istria liberated by Zvonimir

ledger.note: 1074: Zvonimir, then ban, has liberated the Kvarner coast and Istria by the end of Kresimir's reign. The page gives no year for the liberation; the date is the end of his ban (1064/1070-1074, Zvonimir page). Reopened: the Zvonimir page says he and the Hungarian kings Solomon and Geza I 'jointly repelled the Carantanians from Croatia' and that he was ban 1064/1070-1074; still no year for the liberation, so confidence stays 1.

region.text: the Dalmatian cities Zadar, Split, Trogir, Biograd and Nin

ledger.counterpart: Normans of Apulia (Count Amico of Giovinazzo)
ledger.note: 1074: the Normans seize Kresimir and the cities. 'Count Amico of Giovinazzo captured Krešimir, and his ransom required him to surrender many cities, including both capitals, Zadar, Split, and Trogir' (main page: Split, Trogir, Zadar, Biograd, Nin). The Peter Kresimir page puts the invasion in 1075, the main page in 1074; the Zvonimir page has Venice expelling the Normans in February 1075.

region.text: the Dalmatian cities Zadar, Split, Trogir, Biograd and Nin

ledger.note: 1075: Venice expels the Normans and holds the cities. 'In 1075, Venice expelled the Normans and secured the cities for itself'; the Zvonimir page says Zvonimir 'probably helped' and kept authority over Dalmatia 'as far as Osor'. Croatia and Venice both claim the cities until 1085.

region.text: the Dalmatian cities Zadar, Split, Trogir, Biograd and Nin

ledger.note: 1085: Byzantium hands its rights in Dalmatia to Venice. After Zvonimir sent naval help to Robert Guiscard's Normans (1081-1085), 'in 1085, the Byzantines transferred their rights in Dalmatia to Venice.'

union.text: the Kvarner island city-states Krk, Rab and Cres

region.text: the Dalmatian cities (held by Venice since 1075) and the Kvarner islands Krk, Rab and Cres

ledger.note: 1085: Venice holds the Dalmatian cities. 'in 1085, the Byzantines transferred their rights in Dalmatia to Venice.' The cities were already left out of the 1074 keyframe; the islands Krk, Rab and Cres, recognised as Croatian in 1069 and kept through Zvonimir's reign ('authority over Dalmatia ... as far as the distant town of Osor', Zvonimir page), leave the kingdom here with the transfer of the Byzantine rights. The page does not say Croatia lost other land in 1085 although Cliopatria's shape drops 20 thousand km2 (see the verdict; the Zvonimir page, opened a second time, is silent on the east).

region.text: the entire province of Slavonia, north of the Gvozd mountain

ledger.note: 1091: Ladislaus of Hungary conquers Slavonia. 'In 1091 Ladislaus crossed the Drava river and conquered the entire province of Slavonia'; his letter says 'Sclavoniam iam fere totam'. He founds the diocese of Zagreb (undated).

region.text: Croatia south of the Gvozd mountain

ledger.note: 1091: the war for the rest of Croatia begins. Ladislaus appoints his nephew Almos 'to administer the controlled area of Croatia'; the campaign 'was halted near the Gvozd Mountain'; Petar Snacic is elected king in 1093.

region.text: Croatia south of the Gvozd mountain

ledger.note: 1097: Coloman defeats the last native king at Gvozd. 'In 1097 [Coloman] defeated King Petar's troops in the Battle of Gvozd Mountain, where the latter was killed.' Almos had withdrawn to Hungary in 1095.

region.text: the Kingdom of Croatia passing to Coloman of Hungary

ledger.note: 1102: Coloman is crowned king of Croatia at Biograd and Croatia enters union with Hungary. 'Coloman was crowned king of Croatia in Biograd na Moru in 1102.' The Pacta conventa is 'viewed as a 14th-century forgery'. The Conventio Amicitiae of 1098 split the coast between Hungary and Venice (same page).

region.text: the Narentine duchy (Pagania)

ledger.note: 1102: the Narentine vassalage lapses with the kingdom. Page silent on when Pagania ceased to be a vassal; closed at the kingdom's end.

wars.name: Croatian-Bulgarian war of 926
wars.outcome: Croatian victory over Alogobotur's army in 926; peace restored in 927 after Simeon's death through papal legates; no change of border.
wars.note: 'In 926, Simeon tried to break the Croatian-Byzantine pact' (main page).

wars.name: Croatian-Hungarian conflict under Tomislav
wars.outcome: Undated Hungarian war; Croatia kept its northern borders and gained part of the former Pannonian duchy including Sisak.
wars.note: The page cites the Chronicle of the Priest of Duklja for a Croatian victory on the Drava while other sources mention Hungarian wins; year c. 925 only.

wars.name: Venetian expedition and the Dalmatian cities

zones.text: the Dalmatian cities Zadar, Split and Trogir

wars.outcome: Orseolo's fleet takes the eastern Adriatic after 1000; Kresimir III wins back some cities until Venice defeats him in 1018 and Croatia becomes a Byzantine vassal until 1025.

wars.name: Norman invasion of Dalmatia (Amico of Giovinazzo)

zones.text: the Dalmatian cities Zadar, Split, Trogir, Biograd and Nin

wars.outcome: Kresimir IV captured and ransomed with Zadar, Split, Trogir, Biograd and Nin; Venice expels the Normans in February 1075 and keeps the cities.
wars.note: The Peter Kresimir page puts the invasion in 1075, the main page in 1074.

wars.name: Norman invasion of the Byzantine Empire (Guiscard), Croatian naval aid
wars.outcome: Zvonimir, bound by his pledge to the Holy See, sent naval troops to the Normans; in 1085 Byzantium transferred its Dalmatian rights to Venice.
wars.note: No territory is said to change hands in Croatia itself.

wars.name: Hungarian conquest of Croatia
wars.outcome: Ladislaus takes Slavonia in 1091; Almos governs the occupied part until 1095; Petar Snacic is elected king in 1093 and killed at Gvozd in 1097; Coloman is crowned at Biograd in 1102.
wars.note: The Cumans' attack on Hungary halted Ladislaus near the Gvozd; Ladislaus died in 1095.

certainty.note: Medieval Croatia's frontiers in Bosnia, Slavonia and the Dalmatian hinterland are approximate (historians disagree, per the Tomislav page); no treaty line exists. The Dalmatian city-states are the exception only in being distinct places.

notes: Page budget (5) spent on the main article, Tomislav, Peter Kresimir IV, Zvonimir and Coloman. Cliopatria shapes 936-1000 are kept as 'unverified: page budget'; the 980 jump from 55 to 90 thousand km2 is not explained by any page opened. The Byzantine suzerainty over Croatia 1018-1025 ('briefly became a vassal of the Byzantine Empire until 1025', main page) belongs in the byzantine-empire dossier as vassal_start/vassal_end with counterpart kingdom-of-croatia; it is not repeated here because the ledger's vassal events record the suzerain's side. The pages call Zahumlje, Travunia and Duklja within Petar Kresimir IV's 'influence' (1058-1074) without annexation or vassalage; no events are written. The main page's infobox has no end date: 1102 is the coronation year it names (Cliopatria's shape ends 1098). Conventio Amicitiae 1098 (Coloman page): 'split the coast, giving Croatian coastal regions to Hungary and Dalmatia to Venice'; the page is unclear and no ledger event is written. Gazetteer names needed: Pagania (Narentine duchy), Kvarner, Biograd na Moru, Nin, Knin (place), Makarska. Counterparts without dossiers: pagania, Dalmatian city-states, Normans of Apulia, Margraviate of Carniola. Zvonimir page and main page disagree on whether Zvonimir kept Dalmatia (authority 'as far as Osor') or Venice held the cities after 1075; modelled as a contest 1075-1085.
